question: What does the reactivity series of metals represent?
option_1: A list of metals arranged in increasing order of their melting points.
option_2: A list of metals arranged in increasing order of their density.
option_3: A list of metals arranged in decreasing order of their reactivity.
option_4: A list of non-metals arranged by their ability to form ions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A list of metals arranged in decreasing order of their reactivity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reactivity series (activity series) is a list of metals arranged in decreasing order of their chemical reactivity, with the most reactive metal at the top. (सक्रियता श्रेणी — धातुओं की अभिक्रियाशीलता के घटते क्रम में सूची)

 

• The series typically runs: Potassium, Sodium, Calcium, Magnesium, Aluminium, Zinc, Iron, Lead, (Hydrogen), Copper, Silver, Gold — remembered by the mnemonic 'Please Send Cats, Monkeys And Zebras In Large Perfumed Cardboard Coaches, Silently Guarded'.

 

• A more reactive metal can displace a less reactive metal from its salt solution — this is called a displacement reaction, e.g. iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metals above hydrogen in the series can displace hydrogen from dilute acids to form hydrogen gas; metals below hydrogen (like copper, silver, gold) cannot.

 

• The most reactive metals (K, Na) react vigorously even with cold water, while metals like Fe react only with steam, and Cu, Ag, Au do not react with water at all.

 

• Gold and platinum are placed at the very bottom, which is why they are found in a free (native) state in nature and do not corrode easily.

 

NOTE

 

• A list of metals arranged in increasing order of their melting points (Option A): Melting point is a physical property unrelated to the reactivity series.

 

• A list of metals arranged in increasing order of their density (Option B): Density is also a physical property, not the basis of this series.

 

• A list of non-metals arranged by their ability to form ions (Option D): The reactivity series concerns metals, not non-metals.

question:
Match the following connective tissues with their correct features.

a. Areolar tissue — i. fills spaces between organs

b. Skeletal tissues — ii. provide structural support and reduce friction

c. Ligaments — iii. fibrous tissues that maintain muscle-to-bone connection

d. Tendons — iv. fibrous tissues that maintain bone-to-bone connection
option_1: a i, b iv, c ii, d iii
option_2: a iv, b i, c iii, d ii
option_3: a i, b ii, c iv, d iii
option_4: a i, b iv, c iii, d ii
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iv, d-iii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Areolar tissue is a loose connective tissue that fills the spaces between organs and supports internal organs and blood vessels. (एरियोलर ऊतक — अंगों के बीच रिक्त स्थान भरता है)

 

• Skeletal (cartilage) tissue is a supportive connective tissue that provides structural support and reduces friction between bones at joints.

 

• Ligaments are tough, fibrous connective tissues that connect bone to bone, holding the skeletal framework together at joints.

 

• Tendons are strong, inelastic fibrous cords that connect muscle to bone, allowing muscle contraction to move the skeleton.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Connective tissue is one of the four basic animal tissue types, along with epithelial, muscular and nervous tissue, and its main function is to bind and support other tissues and organs.

 

• Blood is a fluid connective tissue in which the matrix (plasma) is liquid, and it transports gases, nutrients and hormones throughout the body.

 

• Adipose tissue is a connective tissue specialised for fat storage and also acts as an insulator against heat loss.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, B and D mismatch either the ligament–tendon pairing or the areolar/skeletal descriptions; remembering 'Ligaments = bone-to-bone' and 'Tendons = muscle-to-bone' is the quickest way to eliminate them.

question: In a multicellular organism, how does each cell support the survival of the organism?
option_1: By converting itself into a complete organ
option_2: By trying to carry out all life functions by itself
option_3: By working independently without interacting with other cells
solution_text:
The correct answer is By following division of labour.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a multicellular organism, different groups of cells are specialised to perform different functions — this is called division of labour. (श्रम विभाजन — बहुकोशिकीय जीवों में कोशिकाओं का विशेषीकरण)

 

• Because of division of labour, cells organise into tissues, tissues into organs, and organs into organ systems, each performing a specific role (e.g. muscle cells contract, nerve cells conduct impulses, red blood cells carry oxygen) so that the organism functions efficiently as a whole.

 

• This specialisation means no single cell needs to perform every life function on its own, unlike a unicellular organism (e.g. Amoeba), where a single cell must carry out nutrition, respiration, excretion and reproduction all by itself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• The basic structural and functional unit of life is the cell, a term coined by Robert Hooke in 1665.

 

• Tissue is a group of similar cells performing a specific function; the study of tissues is called histology.

 

• Examples of division of labour in humans: RBCs transport oxygen, WBCs fight infection, neurons transmit signals, and muscle cells enable movement.

 

NOTE

 

• By converting itself into a complete organ (Option A): A single cell cannot become an entire organ; organs are made of many cells and tissues working together.

 

• By trying to carry out all life functions by itself (Option B): This describes unicellular organisms, not the specialised cells of a multicellular body.

 

• By working independently without interacting with other cells (Option C): Cells in a multicellular organism are highly interdependent, not independent.

question: When sugar is dissolved in water, the particles of sugar:
option_1: get into the spaces between water particles
solution_text:
The correct answer is get into the spaces between water particles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When sugar dissolves in water, the sugar particles move into the spaces (intermolecular gaps) present between the particles of water, forming a homogeneous solution. (विलयन — जल के कणों के बीच रिक्त स्थान में घुलना)

 

• This happens because matter is particulate in nature and has space between its particles; dissolving is a physical change and no new substance is formed, so the sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water.

 

• The particles of sugar do not disappear or vanish — they simply get evenly distributed among the water particles, which is why a sugar solution tastes sweet throughout and is transparent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• This experiment (dissolving substances like sugar, salt, or potassium permanganate in water) is a classic NCERT activity demonstrating that matter is made up of very small particles and that these particles have space between them.

 

• A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances; the substance that dissolves is the solute (sugar) and the one in which it dissolves is the solvent (water).

 

• Diffusion, evaporation and Brownian motion are other everyday phenomena that also demonstrate the particulate and dynamic nature of matter.

 

NOTE

 

• Occupy more space (Option B): Incorrect — the total volume of the solution is usually close to (often slightly less than) the sum of the separate volumes, not more, because sugar particles fill existing gaps.

 

• Disappear permanently (Option C): Incorrect — dissolving is reversible; the sugar can be recovered by evaporating the water, so it has not disappeared, only mixed at the particle level.

 

• Break into smaller pieces only (Option D): Incorrect — dissolving does not involve breaking sugar molecules into smaller pieces; it is simply the intermingling of particles.

question: If an image is formed at the same distance behind a mirror as the object in front, the mirror must be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is plane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a plane mirror, the image formed is always virtual, erect and of the same size as the object, and it is located exactly as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it. (समतल दर्पण — वस्तु जितनी दूरी पर आगे, प्रतिबिंब उतनी ही दूरी पर पीछे)

 

• This equal image-distance property is a defining characteristic of a plane mirror and follows from the laws of reflection, where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection for every ray.

 

• Curved mirrors (concave and convex) do not generally form an image at the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front, because they converge or diverge light rays depending on the object's position relative to the focus and centre of curvature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A concave mirror is converging and can form real, inverted images of varying size (or a virtual, magnified image when the object is within the focal length).

 

• A convex mirror is diverging and always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image, used in vehicle side mirrors and shop security mirrors for a wider field of view.

 

• Lateral inversion (left-right reversal) is a key property of images formed by plane mirrors, as seen when reading text in a mirror.

 

NOTE

 

• Convex (Option A): Always forms a diminished virtual image whose distance behind the mirror is less than the object distance, not equal to it.

 

• Concave (Option C): Image distance varies with object position and can be real or virtual, but is not equal to the object distance in the simple sense described here.

 

• Parabolic (Option D): A parabolic mirror is a special curved mirror (used in headlights/telescopes) and does not have this equal-distance imaging property either.

question: Which of the following chemical secretions helps our body in control and coordination?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hormones.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hormones are chemical messengers secreted directly into the blood by endocrine glands, and together with the nervous system they bring about control and coordination in the body. (हार्मोन — नियंत्रण एवं समन्वय के लिए रासायनिक संदेशवाहक)

 

• Hormones regulate slower, longer-lasting processes such as growth, metabolism, reproduction and the body's response to stress, complementing the nervous system, which controls fast responses through electrical impulses.

 

• Examples: insulin (pancreas) regulates blood sugar, thyroxine (thyroid) regulates metabolism, adrenaline (adrenal gland) prepares the body for 'fight or flight'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The endocrine system, comprising glands like the pituitary, thyroid, adrenal, pancreas and gonads, works alongside the nervous system for overall coordination in the human body.

 

• The pituitary gland, located at the base of the brain, is called the 'master gland' because it controls the secretions of most other endocrine glands.

 

• Plant hormones (auxins, gibberellins, cytokinins) similarly help plants coordinate growth and responses to stimuli, though plants lack a nervous system.

 

NOTE

 

• Sebum (Option A): An oily substance secreted by sebaceous glands in the skin that lubricates skin and hair; it plays no role in control and coordination.

 

• Gastric mucosa (Option C): The lining of the stomach that secretes gastric juices for digestion, not a coordination-related secretion.

 

• Saliva (Option D): A digestive secretion from the salivary glands that begins starch digestion; it is not involved in control and coordination.

question: Which of the following is NOT formed in the chlor-alkali process?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sodium carbonate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The chlor-alkali process is the electrolysis of a saturated aqueous sodium chloride (brine) solution, which produces three useful products: chlorine gas (at the anode), hydrogen gas (at the cathode) and sodium hydroxide (in solution). (क्लोर-क्षार प्रक्रम — Cl₂, H₂ एवं NaOH)

 

• The overall reaction is: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + Cl₂(g) + H₂(g). Since chlorine, hydrogen and sodium hydroxide are all obtained together, the process is named 'chlor-alkali' (chlor = chlorine, alkali = sodium hydroxide).

 

• Sodium carbonate (washing soda, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) is manufactured by a completely different route — the Solvay process — not by electrolysis of brine, so it is not a product of the chlor-alkali process.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uses of chlor-alkali products: Cl₂ is used to make PVC, pesticides and for water treatment/disinfection; H₂ is used in the manufacture of ammonia and as a fuel; NaOH is used in soap and paper manufacturing.

 

• Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂) is prepared by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime — another important application of the chlorine produced in this process.

 

• Sodium carbonate (washing soda) is prepared from sodium chloride by the Solvay (ammonia-soda) process and is used in glass, soap and paper industries, and for removing water hardness.

 

NOTE

 

• Chlorine gas, Sodium hydroxide and Hydrogen gas (Options A, B, C): All three are direct products of the chlor-alkali (electrolysis of brine) process, unlike sodium carbonate.

question: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding sexual reproduction in plant?
option_1: Pollen grain directly travels in the ovary.
option_2: Female germ-cells are present in the ovary.
option_3: Transfer of pollen from one flower to another is achieved by different agents.
option_4: Pollen needs to be transferred from the stamen to the stigma.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pollen grain directly travels in the ovary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pollen grains do not travel directly to the ovary; they first land on the stigma (part of the pistil/carpel), and only then does a pollen tube grow down through the style to reach the ovary and deliver the male gametes. (परागकण — पहले वर्तिकाग्र पर, फिर परागनलिका द्वारा अंडाशय तक)

 

• The female germ-cells (egg cells) are indeed present inside the ovary, within structures called ovules — this statement is correct.

 

• Pollination (transfer of pollen from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another) is carried out by various agents — wind, water, insects and other animals — so this statement is also correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A, as it wrongly states that pollen travels directly into the ovary, skipping the essential stigma-to-ovary journey via the pollen tube.

 

Additional Information

 

• The male reproductive part of a flower is the stamen (anther + filament), producing pollen grains; the female part is the pistil/carpel (stigma + style + ovary), containing the ovules.

 

• After fertilisation, the ovule develops into a seed and the ovary develops into a fruit.

 

• Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or a different flower of the same plant, while cross-pollination occurs between flowers of different plants of the same species.

 

NOTE

 

• Female germ-cells are present in the ovary (Option B): This is a correct statement about plant reproduction, describing the location of the egg cell within the ovule.

 

• Transfer of pollen from one flower to another is achieved by different agents (Option C): Correct — wind, water and insects/animals are the main pollinating agents.

 

• Pollen needs to be transferred from the stamen to the stigma (Option D): Correct — this describes pollination, the essential first step before fertilisation.

question: In which carbon allotrope are atoms arranged in a hexagonal layer structure, with weak forces between layers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Graphite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms in the same plane, forming hexagonal (honeycomb) layers; the different layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, which allow the layers to slide over one another. (ग्रेफाइट — षट्कोणीय परतदार संरचना)

 

• This layered structure with weak inter-layer bonding is why graphite is soft, slippery and a good lubricant/writing material (used in pencils), and it also allows the layers to be exfoliated (as in graphene).

 

• Graphite is also a good conductor of electricity because each carbon atom has one delocalised (free) electron that can move within the layer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diamond, by contrast, has each carbon atom bonded to four other carbon atoms in a rigid three-dimensional tetrahedral network, making it the hardest known natural substance and a poor conductor of electricity.

 

• Graphene, a single isolated layer of graphite's hexagonal carbon sheet, is renowned for extraordinary strength and electrical conductivity and won the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for its discoverers.

 

• Fullerenes (like C₆₀, 'buckyball') are a third crystalline allotrope of carbon, made of carbon atoms arranged in spherical/cage-like structures.

 

NOTE

 

• Diamond (Option A): A rigid, tetrahedral 3-D network, not a layered hexagonal structure.

 

• Coke (Option B): An amorphous (non-crystalline) form of carbon obtained by heating coal, without an ordered hexagonal layer structure.

 

• Fullerene (Option D): Consists of cage-like/spherical carbon molecules, not flat hexagonal layers.

question: A 2 kg body accelerates at 3 m/s². The force acting on it is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6 N.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Newton's Second Law of Motion, force F = mass (m) × acceleration (a). (न्यूटन का द्वितीय नियम — बल = द्रव्यमान × त्वरण)

 

• Given: mass m = 2 kg, acceleration a = 3 m/s².

 

• F = m × a = 2 × 3 = 6 N.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of force is the newton (N), defined as the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a body of mass 1 kg (1 N = 1 kg·m/s²).

 

• Newton's First Law (law of inertia) states a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force.

 

• Newton's Third Law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, C and D (2 N, 3 N, 5 N) come from either misreading the formula or mixing up the given values; always multiply mass and acceleration directly to avoid this error.

question: Which scientist suggested that a magnet exerts an equal and opposite force on a current-carrying conductor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ampere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• André-Marie Ampère showed that just as a current-carrying conductor experiences a force in a magnetic field, the magnet also experiences an equal and opposite force from the current-carrying conductor, consistent with Newton's third law of motion. (एम्पीयर — चुंबक पर धारावाही चालक का समान एवं विपरीत बल)

 

• Ampère's work laid the foundation of electrodynamics, and the SI unit of electric current, the ampere (A), is named in his honour.

 

• He also formulated Ampère's circuital law, relating the integrated magnetic field around a closed loop to the electric current passing through it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hans Christian Oersted discovered in 1820 that a current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field around it, deflecting a nearby compass needle — the starting point of electromagnetism.

 

• Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction — that a changing magnetic field can induce an electric current in a conductor — the principle behind generators and transformers.

 

• James Clerk Maxwell unified electricity, magnetism and optics into a consistent theory through Maxwell's equations, predicting the existence of electromagnetic waves.

 

NOTE

 

• Oersted (Option A): Discovered the magnetic effect of electric current, not the equal-and-opposite force on the magnet.

 

• Maxwell (Option C): Formulated the unified electromagnetic theory, a later theoretical synthesis, not this specific force law.

 

• Faraday (Option D): Known for electromagnetic induction, a different phenomenon from the force between a magnet and a current-carrying conductor.

question: The weight of an object is less on the Moon than on the Earth because:
option_1: the object becomes lighter due to air resistance
option_2: the mass of the object decreases on the Moon
option_3: the moon attracts objects with more force
option_4: the moon has smaller acceleration due to gravity than the Earth
solution_text:
The correct answer is the moon has smaller acceleration due to gravity than the Earth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Weight (W) = mass (m) × acceleration due to gravity (g), i.e. W = mg. (भार = द्रव्यमान × गुरुत्वीय त्वरण)

 

• The Moon's gravitational acceleration is about one-sixth (1/6) of the Earth's (g_moon ≈ 1.63 m/s² vs g_earth ≈ 9.8 m/s²), because the Moon has much smaller mass and radius than the Earth (from g = GM/R²).

 

• Since mass (m) of the object stays the same everywhere, but g is smaller on the Moon, the weight is correspondingly smaller on the Moon — this is why astronauts can jump much higher there.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mass is the quantity of matter in a body and remains constant everywhere in the universe, whereas weight is a force and varies with the value of g at that location.

 

• The Moon has no atmosphere, so there is no air resistance to explain weight loss — ruling out any air-related explanation.

 

• The weightlessness felt by astronauts in orbit is due to free-fall (continuous falling around the Earth), a different phenomenon from the Moon's lower gravity.

 

NOTE

 

• The object becomes lighter due to air resistance (Option A): Incorrect — the Moon has essentially no atmosphere, so air resistance is not a relevant factor at all.

 

• The mass of the object decreases on the Moon (Option B): Incorrect — mass is invariant and does not change with location.

 

• The moon attracts objects with more force (Option C): Incorrect — it is the opposite; the Moon attracts objects with less gravitational force than the Earth.

question: Why are the testes located outside the abdominal cavity in human males?
option_1: Because sperm formation requires a lower temperature than body temperature
option_2: Because sperm formation requires higher temperature
option_3: Because testosterone is produced only outside the body
option_4: To protect them from physical damage
solution_text:
The correct answer is Because sperm formation requires a lower temperature than body temperature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The testes are located outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum, because sperm production (spermatogenesis) requires a temperature slightly lower (about 2-3°C less) than normal body temperature. (वृषण — शुक्राणु निर्माण के लिए शरीर के तापमान से कम तापमान आवश्यक)

 

• The scrotal sac acts as a natural thermoregulator: muscles in its wall can contract or relax to move the testes closer to or farther from the body, helping maintain the optimum lower temperature needed for healthy sperm development.

 

• If the testes remain too close to body-core temperature for extended periods (as in the medical condition cryptorchidism, undescended testes), sperm production is impaired, potentially causing infertility.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The testes perform a dual function: they produce sperm (male gametes) and secrete the hormone testosterone, which controls the development of secondary sexual characteristics in males.

 

• The female equivalent reproductive gland, the ovary, produces eggs (ova) and secretes oestrogen; unlike the testes, the ovaries remain inside the abdominal (pelvic) cavity.

 

• Sperm formed in the testes travel through the vas deferens, mix with secretions from the seminal vesicles and prostate gland, and are ejected through the urethra.

 

NOTE

 

• Because sperm formation requires higher temperature (Option B): Incorrect — it is the opposite; a lower temperature is required, not a higher one.

 

• Because testosterone is produced only outside the body (Option C): Incorrect and physiologically meaningless — hormone production location is not the reason for external placement.

 

• To protect them from physical damage (Option D): Incorrect — this is not the primary biological reason; in fact, the external location makes testes more vulnerable, not less.

question: Which of the following may lead to biological magnification?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pesticides.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biological magnification is the increasing concentration of a non-biodegradable, harmful substance at each successive trophic level of a food chain. (जैव आवर्धन — खाद्य श्रृंखला में हानिकारक पदार्थों का सांद्रण बढ़ना)

 

• Pesticides and chemical fertilisers (e.g. DDT) sprayed on crops are non-biodegradable; they get absorbed by plants, passed on to herbivores that eat those plants, and then further concentrated in the bodies of carnivores that eat the herbivores.

 

• Since each level eats many organisms of the level below, the substance's concentration keeps increasing (magnifying) as it moves up the food chain, reaching the highest concentration in top carnivores, including humans.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is the classic textbook example of a biomagnified pesticide, historically causing eggshell thinning in birds of prey.

 

• Substances causing biomagnification must be fat-soluble and non-biodegradable, so they accumulate in body tissues rather than being excreted or broken down.

 

• Biodegradable wastes (like vegetable peels, straw, and other organic matter) are broken down by decomposers (bacteria and fungi) into simpler substances and do not biomagnify.

 

NOTE

 

• Degrading vegetables (Option A): Being biodegradable, they are decomposed naturally and do not accumulate in food chains.

 

• Peel of banana (Option C): A biodegradable organic waste that decomposes readily and poses no biomagnification risk.

 

• Straw (Option D): Also biodegradable plant waste, easily broken down by decomposers, unlike persistent chemical pesticides.

question: Which of the following decomposes on heating to give quick lime?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaCO3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Calcium carbonate (CaCO₃), commonly known as limestone, undergoes thermal decomposition on strong heating to form calcium oxide (CaO, quicklime) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas. (चूना पत्थर का अपघटन — CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂)

 

• The reaction is: CaCO₃ (heat) → CaO + CO₂. This is an important example of a decomposition reaction, where a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler products on heating.

 

• Quicklime (CaO) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime, Ca(OH)₂, releasing a large amount of heat — a reaction used in whitewashing and in the manufacture of cement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Calcium carbonate occurs naturally as limestone, marble and chalk, and is also the main component of eggshells and seashells.

 

• Slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) solution, called limewater, turns milky when carbon dioxide is passed through it, due to formation of insoluble CaCO₃ — a standard test for CO₂.

 

• Other classic thermal decomposition examples: ferrous sulphate (FeSO₄) decomposes on heating to give Fe₂O₃, SO₂ and SO₃; lead nitrate decomposes to give PbO, NO₂ and O₂.

 

NOTE

 

• CaCl (Option A): Not a standard stable compound in this context (calcium typically forms CaCl₂); it does not decompose to give quicklime.

 

• KClO₃ (Option C): Potassium chlorate decomposes on heating to give potassium chloride and oxygen gas, not quicklime.

 

• NaOH (Option D): Sodium hydroxide is a stable alkali and does not decompose on ordinary heating to give quicklime.

question: Which of the following statements about sexual reproduction is INCORRECT?
option_1: It generates variations for species survival.
option_2: It helps organisms adapt to changing environments.
option_4: It combines DNA from two parents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It produces identical clones.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sexual reproduction involves the fusion of male and female gametes (each carrying DNA from one parent) to form a zygote, so the offspring receives a combination of genetic material from two parents, making it genetically different from both parents. (लैंगिक जनन — दो जनकों के DNA का संयोजन, विविधता उत्पन्न करता है)

 

• Because of this genetic recombination, sexual reproduction generates variations among offspring, which is essential for a species' ability to adapt to a changing environment and for its long-term survival through natural selection.

 

• Identical clones (offspring genetically identical to a single parent) are instead a hallmark of asexual reproduction (e.g. binary fission, budding, vegetative propagation), where there is no mixing of genetic material from two parents.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C, as it incorrectly attributes clone production to sexual reproduction.

 

Additional Information

 

• Asexual reproduction methods include binary fission (Amoeba), budding (Hydra, yeast), fragmentation (Spirogyra), spore formation (Rhizopus/bread mould) and vegetative propagation (potato, rose).

 

• Genetic variation from sexual reproduction is the raw material for evolution, as favourable variations may help a species survive environmental changes.

 

• In humans, meiosis during gamete formation and the random fusion of sperm and egg are key sources of genetic variation.

 

NOTE

 

• It generates variations for species survival (Option A): A correct and defining feature of sexual reproduction.

 

• It helps organisms adapt to changing environments (Option B): Correct — variation is the basis for adaptation via natural selection.

 

• It combines DNA from two parents (Option D): Correct — this fusion of two parental genomes is the essence of sexual reproduction.

question:
A rifle fires a light bullet, resulting in a large forward acceleration of the bullet and a

minimal backward recoil acceleration of the rifle. If the forces are equal and opposite

(Action/Reaction), why is the rifle's acceleration so much smaller than the bullet's?
option_1: The acceleration is inversely proportional to the mass, and the rifle has a much greater mass than the bullet.
option_2: The reaction force of the bullet acts for a shorter duration than the action force.
option_3: Action and reaction forces cancel out since they act instantaneously.
option_4: The action force of the rifle on the bullet is greater than the reaction force of the bullet on the rifle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The acceleration is inversely proportional to the mass, and the rifle has a much greater mass than the bullet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• By Newton's third law, the force the rifle exerts on the bullet and the force the bullet exerts on the rifle (recoil) are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. (न्यूटन का तृतीय नियम — क्रिया-प्रतिक्रिया बल बराबर परन्तु त्वरण भिन्न)

 

• However, by Newton's second law, a = F/m, acceleration is inversely proportional to mass for a given force. Since the rifle's mass is far greater than the bullet's mass, the same magnitude of force produces a much smaller acceleration in the rifle than in the bullet.

 

• This is why the bullet shoots forward at high speed while the rifle only recoils slightly (with a gentle 'kick' felt by the shooter), even though the forces on both are equal and opposite.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's third law action-reaction pairs act on different bodies (bullet and rifle here), so they never cancel each other out for a single object.

 

• Other everyday examples of action-reaction pairs: a swimmer pushing water backward to move forward, or a rocket expelling gas downward to move upward.

 

• Momentum is conserved in this system: the small mass of the bullet moving fast and the large mass of the rifle moving slow have momenta of equal magnitude and opposite direction.

 

NOTE

 

• The reaction force acts for a shorter duration than the action force (Option B): Incorrect — action and reaction forces always act for the same duration (they occur simultaneously as a pair).

 

• Action and reaction forces cancel out since they act instantaneously (Option C): Incorrect — action-reaction forces act on different objects, so they never cancel; they only cancel if acting on the same object, which is not the case here.

 

• The action force of the rifle on the bullet is greater than the reaction force (Option D): Incorrect — by Newton's third law, the two forces are always exactly equal in magnitude, never unequal.

question: Which gland secretes the growth hormone (GH) in humans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pituitary gland.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The growth hormone (GH), also called somatotropin, is secreted by the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, and it regulates the growth of bones and muscles in the body. (वृद्धि हार्मोन — पीयूष ग्रंथि द्वारा स्रावित)

 

• The pituitary gland is a small, pea-sized gland situated at the base of the brain, and is often called the 'master gland' because it also controls the secretions of several other endocrine glands.

 

• Deficiency of growth hormone in childhood causes dwarfism, while its excess causes gigantism in children and acromegaly in adults (after bone growth plates have fused).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important pituitary hormones include prolactin (milk production), ADH/vasopressin (water reabsorption in kidneys), oxytocin (uterine contractions during childbirth) and TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH (which stimulate other endocrine glands).

 

• The pancreas secretes insulin and glucagon, which regulate blood glucose levels, and is both an endocrine and exocrine gland.

 

• The thyroid gland secretes thyroxine, which regulates the body's basal metabolic rate, while the adrenal glands secrete adrenaline (fight-or-flight response) and corticosteroids.

 

NOTE

 

• Pancreas (Option A): Secretes insulin/glucagon for blood sugar regulation, not growth hormone.

 

• Thyroid gland (Option C): Secretes thyroxine, controlling metabolism, not growth hormone.

 

• Adrenal gland (Option D): Secretes adrenaline and corticosteroids for stress response, not growth hormone.

question:
Rutherford's gold foil experiment led to a major revision of the atomic model. Which of

the following observations and conclusions is most accurate according to the

experiment?
option_1: Electrons are present in the nucleus and account for the atom's mass.
option_2: Alpha particles are deflected because they collide with electrons and spread uniformly throughout the atom.
option_3: The nucleus is positively charged and occupies most of the volume of the atom.
option_4: The majority of alpha particles passed through the foil undeflected, indicating that atoms are mostly empty space.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The majority of alpha particles passed through the foil undeflected, indicating that atoms are mostly empty space.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Rutherford's alpha-particle scattering (gold foil) experiment (1911), a beam of alpha particles was directed at a thin gold foil, and it was observed that most of the alpha particles passed straight through undeflected, while only a very small fraction were deflected at large angles (and a tiny fraction even bounced straight back). (रदरफोर्ड का स्वर्ण पत्र प्रयोग — परमाणु में अधिकांश भाग खाली स्थान)

 

• The fact that most particles went straight through led Rutherford to conclude that most of the atom is empty space.

 

• The rare large-angle deflections showed that there is a tiny, dense, positively charged centre — the nucleus — where nearly all the mass is concentrated, and electrons revolve around it at a distance, in mostly empty space.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rutherford's model is called the 'nuclear model' or 'planetary model' of the atom, replacing J.J. Thomson's earlier 'plum pudding model', in which positive charge was thought to be spread evenly throughout the atom with embedded electrons.

 

• A key limitation of Rutherford's model was that it could not explain why orbiting electrons do not lose energy and spiral into the nucleus — this was later addressed by Niels Bohr's model, which introduced fixed energy orbits (shells).

 

• The gold foil was chosen because gold can be beaten into extremely thin sheets, allowing the alpha particles to interact with only a few layers of atoms.

 

NOTE

 

• Electrons are present in the nucleus and account for the atom's mass (Option A): Incorrect — electrons are extremely light and orbit outside the nucleus; the nucleus's mass comes from protons and neutrons, not electrons.

 

• Alpha particles are deflected because they collide with electrons and spread uniformly throughout the atom (Option B): Incorrect — this describes Thomson's (disproven) plum-pudding idea, not Rutherford's conclusion; deflection is due to the concentrated positive nucleus, not electron collisions.

 

• The nucleus is positively charged and occupies most of the volume of the atom (Option C): Incorrect in part — the nucleus is indeed positively charged, but it occupies an extremely tiny fraction of the atom's volume, not most of it.

question:
Which of the following is the correct formula for kinetic energy of a body of mass 'm' kg

moving with a uniform speed of 'v' m/s?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1/2 mv2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kinetic energy (KE) is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion, and is given by the formula KE = 1/2 × m × v², where m is mass and v is velocity (speed). (गतिज ऊर्जा = 1/2 × द्रव्यमान × वेग²)

 

• This formula is derived using the work-energy theorem: the work done to accelerate a body of mass m from rest to velocity v equals the kinetic energy it gains, W = F × s = ma × s, which simplifies to (1/2)mv² using the equations of motion.

 

• Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity and its SI unit is the joule (J), same as the unit for work and all other forms of energy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Momentum (p = mv) is a different quantity — a vector — related to but distinct from kinetic energy; KE can also be written as KE = p²/2m.

 

• Potential energy due to gravity is given by PE = mgh, where h is height above a reference level; the sum of KE and PE is called mechanical energy, conserved in the absence of friction.

 

• Doubling the velocity of a body quadruples its kinetic energy (since KE ∝ v²), which is why high-speed collisions are far more destructive than low-speed ones.

 

NOTE

 

• 1/4 mv2 (Option A): An incorrect coefficient; the correct factor in the KE formula is 1/2, not 1/4.

 

• mv (Option B): This is the formula for momentum, not kinetic energy.

 

• 1/2 mv (Option C): Missing the square on velocity; without squaring v, this does not represent kinetic energy.

question:
Which of the following is a common characteristic of both acids and bases when

dissolved in water?
option_1: Both produce carbon dioxide when reacted with metal carbonates.
option_2: Both release hydrogen gas on reacting with metals like zinc.
option_4: Both produce ions that conduct electricity in aqueous solutions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both produce ions that conduct electricity in aqueous solutions.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When dissolved in water, acids ionise to produce H⁺ (H₃O⁺) ions, and bases (alkalis) ionise to produce OH⁻ ions; in both cases, the presence of free-moving ions in solution allows the solution to conduct electricity. (अम्ल एवं क्षार — जलीय विलयन में आयन बनाकर विद्युत का चालन)

 

• This is why aqueous solutions of both acids (like HCl) and bases (like NaOH) are good conductors, and this property is used to test for the presence of ions in the Arrhenius theory of acids and bases.

 

• In contrast, reactions with metal carbonates or with reactive metals like zinc, and effects on litmus, are properties specific to acids only, not shared by bases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acids turn blue litmus red, react with active metals to release hydrogen gas (e.g. Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂), and react with metal carbonates/bicarbonates to release CO₂ (e.g. Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂).

 

• Bases turn red litmus blue, feel soapy/slippery, and react with acids in a neutralisation reaction to form salt and water.

 

• The pH scale (0–14), devised by S.P.L. Sorensen, is used to measure the strength of acidity or alkalinity of a solution; pH 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.

 

NOTE

 

• Both produce carbon dioxide when reacted with metal carbonates (Option A): Incorrect — this reaction is characteristic of acids only; bases do not typically react with carbonates to release CO₂.

 

• Both release hydrogen gas on reacting with metals like zinc (Option B): Incorrect — only acids (and strong bases in some special cases like NaOH with Zn/Al) typically show this, but it is primarily an acid-metal reaction, not a shared general property in the way stated.

 

• Both turn blue litmus red (Option C): Incorrect — only acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue, the opposite effect.

question: Conditions to liquefy gases would be:
solution_text:
The correct answer is increasing pressure and decreasing temperature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gases can be liquefied by increasing the pressure (which pushes particles closer together) and decreasing the temperature (which reduces the kinetic energy of particles, weakening their tendency to move apart). (गैस द्रवीकरण — दाब बढ़ाकर एवं तापमान घटाकर)

 

• As particles come closer together and slow down, the intermolecular forces of attraction become strong enough to hold them in the liquid state, causing the gas to condense into a liquid.

 

• This principle is used industrially to liquefy gases such as LPG (liquefied petroleum gas), oxygen, and nitrogen, by applying high pressure combined with low temperature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The interconversion of states of matter (solid ⇌ liquid ⇌ gas) can be achieved by changing temperature and pressure; increasing temperature and decreasing pressure favours the gaseous state, while the reverse favours the liquid/solid state.

 

• Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into a gas (or vice versa) without passing through the liquid state, e.g. camphor, naphthalene, dry ice (solid CO₂).

 

• The kinetic theory of matter explains that particles in a gas have the most energy and greatest spacing, and cooling/compressing them reduces both energy and spacing, forcing a phase change.

 

NOTE

 

• Increasing pressure and increasing temperature (Option A): Incorrect — increasing temperature works against liquefaction by increasing particle motion, opposing the effect of increased pressure.

 

• Decreasing pressure and decreasing temperature (Option B): Incorrect — decreasing pressure allows particles to move further apart, opposing liquefaction even though lower temperature helps.

 

• Decreasing pressure and increasing temperature (Option D): Incorrect — both these changes favour the gaseous state, making liquefaction less likely, not more.

question:
In the case of a convex mirror, a ray parallel to the principal axis after reflection appears

to diverge from:
solution_text:
The correct answer is The principal focus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a convex mirror, a ray of light travelling parallel to the principal axis, after reflection from the mirror's surface, appears to diverge (spread out) from a point behind the mirror — this point is the principal focus (F). (उत्तल दर्पण — मुख्य अक्ष के समांतर किरण, फोकस से अपसरित होती प्रतीत होती है)

 

• Since a convex mirror is a diverging mirror, the reflected rays never actually meet; when extended backward, they appear to originate from the virtual focus located behind the mirror.

 

• This is one of the standard rules for ray diagrams in convex mirrors, essential for constructing images and understanding why convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, diminished images.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other standard ray rule for convex mirrors: a ray directed towards the centre of curvature (or its virtual extension) hits the mirror normally and reflects back along the same path.

 

• A ray directed towards the principal focus (behind the mirror) becomes parallel to the principal axis after reflection — the reverse of the first rule.

 

• Convex mirrors are widely used as rear-view/side mirrors in vehicles and in shops for security, because they provide a wider field of view than plane mirrors.

 

NOTE

 

• The pole (Option A): The pole is the centre point of the mirror's reflecting surface, used as a reference for measuring distances, not the point of apparent divergence of parallel rays.

 

• The centre of curvature (Option C): This is the centre of the sphere of which the mirror is a part; rays through it reflect straight back, unrelated to parallel-ray behaviour.

 

• Infinity (Option D): Rays converging from or heading to infinity describe an object/image at infinity, not the reflection behaviour of a parallel ray off a convex mirror.

question:
Which of the following is correct about force on a current-carrying conductor in a

magnetic field?
option_1: The force is independent of the current in the conductor.
option_2: The force on a current carrying conductor is proportional to the length of the conductor in the magnetic field.
option_3: The force depends on the resistance of the conductor.
option_4: The force on a conductor is along the magnetic field direction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The force on a current carrying conductor is proportional to the length of the conductor in the magnetic field.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The magnetic force on a straight current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field is given by F = BIL sinθ, where B is the magnetic field strength, I is the current, L is the length of the conductor in the field, and θ is the angle between the conductor and the field. (धारावाही चालक पर बल — F = BIL sinθ, लंबाई के समानुपाती)

 

• From this formula, it is clear that the force F is directly proportional to the length (L) of the conductor within the magnetic field — a longer conductor carrying the same current experiences a proportionally larger force.

 

• The force is maximum when the conductor is placed perpendicular to the field (θ = 90°) and zero when placed parallel to the field (θ = 0°).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The direction of this force is given by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: if the forefinger points along the field, the middle finger along the current, then the thumb gives the direction of the force — and this force is always perpendicular to both the current and the magnetic field, not along the field direction.

 

• This force (F = BIL sinθ) is the fundamental principle behind the working of an electric motor, which converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

 

• The related phenomenon in reverse — a moving conductor inducing an EMF in a magnetic field — is the basis of an electric generator, governed by Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction.

 

NOTE

 

• The force is independent of the current in the conductor (Option A): Incorrect — from F = BIL sinθ, the force is directly proportional to the current I, not independent of it.

 

• The force depends on the resistance of the conductor (Option C): Incorrect — the magnetic force formula F = BIL sinθ does not involve the conductor's resistance at all.

 

• The force on a conductor is along the magnetic field direction (Option D): Incorrect — by Fleming's left-hand rule, the force is perpendicular to the magnetic field (and to the current), not along it.

question: Which of the following will NOT produce an echo?
option_3: A tall building at 30 m distance
solution_text:
The correct answer is A wall at 10 m distance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For an echo to be heard distinctly, the reflected sound must reach the ear at least 0.1 second after the original sound (since the sensation of sound persists in the human ear for about 0.1 s). (प्रतिध्वनि हेतु न्यूनतम दूरी — लगभग 17.2 मीटर)

 

• Taking the speed of sound in air as v ≈ 344 m/s, the minimum distance of the reflecting surface is: distance = (v × t)/2 = (344 × 0.1)/2 = 17.2 metres (the sound must travel to the surface and back, hence division by 2).

 

• A reflecting surface at 10 m is less than this minimum distance of 17.2 m, so the reflected sound reaches the ear too soon (in less than 0.1 s) and merges with the original sound — no distinct echo is heard.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Surfaces at 30 m, 50 m and 100 m are all well beyond the minimum 17.2 m threshold, so clear, distinctly audible echoes are produced from these distances.

 

• Reverberation is a related phenomenon — the persistence of sound due to multiple reflections in an enclosed space — commonly experienced in large halls and auditoriums.

 

• Applications of the reflection of sound include SONAR (measuring sea depth), stethoscopes, megaphones and ultrasound imaging in medicine.

 

NOTE

 

• A cliff at 100 m, a tall building at 30 m, and a mountain at 50 m distance (Options B, C, D): All these distances comfortably exceed the 17.2 m minimum required for an echo, so all of them will produce an audible echo, unlike the 10 m wall.

question:
A and B working together can complete a piece of work in 2 days. B alone can complete

the same work in 10 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to complete double the

work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• (A + B)'s 1 day work = 1/2. B's 1 day work = 1/10.

 

SOLUTION

 

• A's 1 day work = (A+B)'s work − B's work = 1/2 − 1/10 = 5/10 − 1/10 = 4/10 = 2/5.

 

• So A alone completes 1 (single) work in 5/2 = 2.5 days.

 

• Time for A to complete double the work = 2 × 2.5 = 5 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• (A+B)'s efficiency − B's efficiency = A's efficiency. Use LCM method: let total work = 10 units. (A+B) rate = 10/2 = 5 units/day; B rate = 10/10 = 1 unit/day; A rate = 4 units/day. Double work = 20 units ÷ 4 = 5 days.

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract efficiencies (work/day), not the number of days, when combining or removing workers from a team.

question:
The average age of 37 students of a class is 42 years. If the age of the teacher is also

included, the average age of the whole group becomes 43 years. The age (in years) of

the teacher is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 80.

 

GIVEN

 

• Average age of 37 students = 42 years. Average age of 37 students + teacher = 43 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total age of 37 students = 37 × 42 = 1554 years.

 

• Total age of 38 people (students + teacher) = 38 × 43 = 1634 years.

 

• Age of teacher = 1634 − 1554 = 80 years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Teacher's age = old average + (number of students × increase in average) = 42 + (37 × 1) = 42 + 38 = 80. (The +1 rise is shared: 37 students each 'gain' 1, plus the new average itself, giving 38.)

 

NOTE

 

• Sum = average × number of people; always convert averages to totals before adding or removing a member.

question:
If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 12% and its height is

increased by 169%, then what is the percentage increase (closest integer) in its

volume?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 108%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Radius decreases by 12% (new r = 0.88r). Height increases by 169% (new h = 2.69h).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Volume of cylinder V = πr²h. New volume V' = π(0.88r)²(2.69h) = π r² h × (0.88)² × 2.69.

 

• (0.88)² = 0.7744. New volume factor = 0.7744 × 2.69 = 2.083136.

 

• Percentage increase = (2.083136 − 1) × 100 = 108.31% ≈ 108%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use the percentage-multiplying-factor method: r-factor = 0.88, r²-factor = 0.7744, h-factor = 2.69; multiply all factors (0.7744 × 2.69 ≈ 2.083) and subtract 1, then convert to %.

 

NOTE

 

• For volume-type problems with %change in multiple dimensions, always multiply the (1 ± %) factors of each dimension (squaring the factor for radius, since V ∝ r²h) rather than adding percentages directly.

question:
Simplify :

(1 − sec x) / (cosec x · cot x)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. (cosx − 1)tan²x.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (1 − sec x) / (cosec x · cot x).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Numerator: 1 − sec x = 1 − 1/cos x = (cos x − 1)/cos x.

 

• Denominator: cosec x · cot x = (1/sin x) × (cos x/sin x) = cos x/sin²x.

 

• Dividing: [(cos x − 1)/cos x] ÷ [cos x/sin²x] = (cos x − 1)/cos x × sin²x/cos x = (cos x − 1) × (sin²x/cos²x) = (cos x − 1)tan²x.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert everything to sin x and cos x first — this almost always simplifies trigonometric expressions fastest; then recognise sin²x/cos²x = tan²x to finish quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Common identities used here: sec x = 1/cos x, cosec x = 1/sin x, cot x = cos x/sin x, and tan x = sin x/cos x. Memorising these conversions is essential for all trig simplification questions.

question:
If 5/13 of a certain number is added to 7/39 of the same number, the result is 132. Find

the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 234.

 

GIVEN

 

• 5/13 of a number + 7/39 of the same number = 132.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take LCM of 13 and 39 = 39. 5/13 = 15/39.

 

• 15/39 + 7/39 = 22/39 of the number = 132.

 

• Number = 132 × 39/22 = 132/22 × 39 = 6 × 39 = 234.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine the fractions first (15/39 + 7/39 = 22/39), then multiply the given result by the reciprocal (39/22) to isolate the number directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always express all fractions with a common denominator before adding, especially when they represent parts of the same unknown quantity.

question:
The cost of a washing machine is 50% less than the cost of a TV. If the cost of the

washing machine increases by 76% and that of the TV decreases by 28%, then what is

the percentage change in the total cost of 4 washing machines and 2 TVs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Increase by 24%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Washing machine (WM) cost is 50% less than TV cost. WM cost increases 76%; TV cost decreases 28%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let TV cost = ₹100, so WM cost = ₹50 (50% less than TV).

 

• Original total of 4 WM + 2 TV = 4(50) + 2(100) = 200 + 200 = ₹400.

 

• New WM cost = 50 × 1.76 = ₹88. New TV cost = 100 × 0.72 = ₹72.

 

• New total = 4(88) + 2(72) = 352 + 144 = ₹496.

 

• % change = (496 − 400)/400 × 100 = 96/400 × 100 = 24% increase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume convenient round values (TV = 100, WM = 50) to convert percentages into actual numbers instantly, then compute the overall % change on the combined total.

 

NOTE

 

• When items are combined in different quantities and change by different percentages, always compute the actual weighted totals — you cannot simply average the two percentage changes.

question: A cycle is sold for ₹2,700 at a loss of 10%. Find its cost price.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹3,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling price (SP) = ₹2,700. Loss = 10%.

 

SOLUTION

 

• When there is a loss of 10%, SP = 90% of CP, i.e. SP = 0.9 × CP.

 

• CP = SP / 0.9 = 2700 / 0.9 = ₹3,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• CP = SP × 100/(100 − loss%) = 2700 × 100/90 = 2700 × 10/9 = 3000.

 

NOTE

 

• For a loss, always divide SP by (100 − loss%)/100; for a profit, divide SP by (100 + profit%)/100. Never subtract/add the percentage directly to SP.

question:
The sides of a triangle are 68 cm, 31 cm, and 87 cm. What is the length of its altitude

corresponding to the side with a length of 31 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 60 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• Sides of triangle: a = 68 cm, b = 31 cm, c = 87 cm.

 

SOLUTION (Heron's formula, then Area = ½ × base × height)

 

• Semi-perimeter s = (68 + 31 + 87)/2 = 186/2 = 93.

 

• Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] = √[93 × 25 × 62 × 6] = √864900 = 930 cm².

 

• Using the side 31 cm as the base: Area = ½ × base × height ⇒ 930 = ½ × 31 × h ⇒ h = 1860/31 = 60 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Area = ½ × base × corresponding altitude for ANY choice of base — once Area is found via Heron's formula, altitude to any given side = 2 × Area ÷ that side.

 

NOTE

 

• Different sides give different altitudes for the same triangle; always divide by the specific side named in the question (here 31 cm), not any other side.

question:
An uncle is 6 times as old as his nephew. In 6 years, the difference in their ages will be

30 years. What is the sum of their current ages (in years)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 42.

 

GIVEN

 

• Uncle's age = 6 × nephew's age (currently). Age difference after 6 years = 30 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let nephew's current age = n. Uncle's current age = 6n.

 

• The difference in ages never changes with time, so current difference = 6n − n = 5n = 30 ⇒ n = 6.

 

• Uncle's age = 6 × 6 = 36. Nephew's age = 6.

 

• Sum of current ages = 36 + 6 = 42.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• The age difference given 'after X years' is the SAME as the current age difference — this is the key shortcut in nearly all such age problems; solve directly using 5n = 30.

 

NOTE

 

• A very common trap here is to try to use the '6 years later' detail to compute future ages — but the difference in ages is constant, so it directly gives the current age gap.

question:
The data 30, 33, 49, 51, x, x+4, 73, 79, 85, 96 is arranged in the ascending order and the

median of the data is 64.

Find the value of x.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 62.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ascending data (10 values): 30, 33, 49, 51, x, x+4, 73, 79, 85, 96. Median = 64.

 

SOLUTION

 

• For 10 (even number of) observations, median = average of the 5th and 6th terms.

 

• 5th term = x, 6th term = x + 4.

 

• Median = (x + x + 4)/2 = (2x + 4)/2 = x + 2.

 

• x + 2 = 64 ⇒ x = 62.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For an even count of data, median = (sum of the two middle terms)/2; just identify the two middle terms by position (n/2 and n/2 + 1) and set up the equation directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check that the data set is genuinely in ascending order after substituting x = 62 (so x = 62 and x+4 = 66 lie correctly between 51 and 73) — it does, confirming the answer is consistent.

question: If the ratio of two numbers is 2 : 5, and their HCF is 29, then their LCM is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 290.

 

GIVEN

 

• Ratio of two numbers = 2 : 5. HCF = 29.

 

SOLUTION

 

• When two numbers are in ratio a : b with HCF = h, the numbers are (a × h) and (b × h), i.e. 2 × 29 = 58 and 5 × 29 = 145.

 

• LCM of numbers in ratio a : b (in lowest terms) with HCF h is simply a × b × h = 2 × 5 × 29 = 290.

 

• Check: LCM × HCF = product of numbers ⇒ 290 × 29 = 8410, and 58 × 145 = 8410. ✓

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two numbers are in ratio a : b (co-prime a, b) with HCF = h: LCM = a × b × h directly, no need to find the actual numbers first.

 

NOTE

 

• This shortcut works only when a and b (the ratio terms) are co-prime to each other, which is the standard case in such ratio-HCF-LCM problems.

question:
Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 110 km/hr and 150 km/hr. The

length of one train is 500 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 10 seconds.

The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 222.22 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Speeds: 110 km/hr and 150 km/hr (opposite directions). One train's length = 500 m. Time to cross each other = 10 seconds.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Relative speed (opposite directions) = 110 + 150 = 260 km/hr = 260 × 5/18 m/s = 1300/18 = 72.222 m/s.

 

• Total distance covered while crossing = relative speed × time = 72.222 × 10 = 722.22 m.

 

• This total distance equals the sum of both train lengths: 500 + L = 722.22 ⇒ L = 222.22 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert km/hr to m/s using ×5/18; for two trains crossing each other, (sum of speeds) × time = (sum of lengths) — always use sum for opposite direction, difference for same direction.

 

NOTE

 

• The option text in the answer key appears with a rendering glitch (e.g. 'C).22' for the value 222.22); the underlying correct numeric value is 222.22 m as derived above.

question: Simplify: [24 − {6 + 3² − (4 × 2 + 1)}] ÷ 3 + 5 × 2
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 17.

 

GIVEN

 

• [24 − {6 + 3² − (4 × 2 + 1)}] ÷ 3 + 5 × 2 = ?

 

SOLUTION (VBODMAS: innermost bracket → curly bracket → square bracket → ÷/× → +/−)

 

• Innermost parentheses: (4 × 2 + 1) = (8 + 1) = 9.

 

• Curly bracket: {6 + 3² − 9}. As per this question's official answer key, the working treats the '3²' term as contributing 6 to the sum at this step, giving {6 + 6 − 9} = 3.

 

• Square bracket: [24 − 3] = 21.

 

• 21 ÷ 3 = 7. Then 7 + 5 × 2 = 7 + 10 = 17.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A (as per the official answer key).

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Resolve brackets strictly from the innermost outward, and always finish all multiplication/division before the final addition/subtraction (BODMAS/VBODMAS order).

 

NOTE

 

• IMPORTANT: applying standard order of operations literally (3² = 9) to [24 − {6 + 3² − (4×2+1)}] ÷ 3 + 5 × 2 gives {6+9−9}=6, [24−6]=18, 18÷3=6, 6+5×2=16 (Option D). This is a known discrepancy between the strict mathematical evaluation and this question's marked key (Option A/17), most likely because the key's working used 6 in place of 3²=9 at that step. This answer sheet follows the officially marked key (Option A) as instructed; students should be aware standard BODMAS on the printed expression yields 16.

question: Simplify: (3x − 2)² − (x + 4)²
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 8x² − 20x − 12.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (3x − 2)² − (x + 4)².

 

SOLUTION

 

• Expand (3x − 2)² = 9x² − 12x + 4 (using (a−b)² = a² − 2ab + b², a=3x, b=2).

 

• Expand (x + 4)² = x² + 8x + 16 (using (a+b)² = a² + 2ab + b²).

 

• Subtract: (9x² − 12x + 4) − (x² + 8x + 16) = 9x² − 12x + 4 − x² − 8x − 16.

 

• Combine like terms: (9x² − x²) + (−12x − 8x) + (4 − 16) = 8x² − 20x − 12.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Alternatively use a² − b² = (a−b)(a+b) with a = (3x−2), b = (x+4): (a−b) = 2x−6, (a+b) = 4x+2, product = (2x−6)(4x+2) = 8x² +4x −24x −12 = 8x² −20x −12 — same result, often faster.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch signs carefully when subtracting an entire squared bracket — every term inside the second bracket must have its sign flipped before combining.

question:
A shopkeeper marks the price of an article at ₹1,980. Find the cost price if after allowing

a discount of 12% he still gains 32% on the cost price.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹1,320.

 

GIVEN

 

• Marked price (MP) = ₹1,980. Discount = 12%. Profit = 32% on cost price.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Selling price (SP) = MP × (1 − discount%) = 1980 × 0.88 = ₹1,742.4.

 

• Since profit is 32% on CP: SP = 1.32 × CP ⇒ CP = SP / 1.32 = 1742.4 / 1.32 = ₹1,320.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• CP = MP × (1 − discount%) / (1 + profit%) = 1980 × 0.88 / 1.32 = 1980 × (0.88/1.32) = 1980 × (2/3) = 1320.

 

NOTE

 

• Always apply discount on the Marked Price to get SP first, and profit/loss % is always calculated on the Cost Price — never mix up the base for each percentage.

question:
Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7.5% per annum, respectively. Mukund

borrowed an amount of ₹2,00,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹)

between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Mukund after 2 years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ₹16,000.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal from each bank = ₹2,00,000. Rate A = 3.5% p.a.; Rate B = 7.5% p.a. Time = 2 years.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Simple Interest formula: SI = P × R × T / 100.

 

• SI to Bank A = 2,00,000 × 3.5 × 2 / 100 = ₹14,000.

 

• SI to Bank B = 2,00,000 × 7.5 × 2 / 100 = ₹30,000.

 

• Positive difference = 30,000 − 14,000 = ₹16,000.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since principal and time are the same for both loans, the difference in SI depends only on the rate difference: SI difference = P × (R2 − R1) × T/100 = 2,00,000 × (7.5−3.5) × 2/100 = 2,00,000 × 4 × 2/100 = 16,000.

 

NOTE

 

• When principal and time are identical for two rates, always shortcut by computing the difference in rates first, rather than calculating each SI separately.

question:
When x is added to each of 17, 9, 26 and 14, then the numbers so obtained, in this order,

are in proportion. Then, if 8x : y :: y : (4x−2), and y > 0, what is the value of y?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 4.

 

GIVEN

 

• (17+x), (9+x), (26+x), (14+x) are in proportion. Also 8x : y :: y : (4x−2), y > 0.

 

SOLUTION

 

• In proportion: (17+x)/(9+x) = (26+x)/(14+x).

 

• Cross-multiplying: (17+x)(14+x) = (9+x)(26+x).

 

• LHS = 238 + 31x + x². RHS = 234 + 35x + x².

 

• 238 + 31x = 234 + 35x ⇒ 238 − 234 = 35x − 31x ⇒ 4 = 4x ⇒ x = 1.

 

• Now 8x = 8, and 4x − 2 = 4(1) − 2 = 2.

 

• Given 8x : y :: y : (4x−2) means y² = 8x × (4x−2) = 8 × 2 = 16 ⇒ y = √16 = 4 (taking y > 0).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In any proportion a : b :: c : d, product of extremes = product of means (a×d = b×c); for a mean proportional a : y :: y : d, always use y² = a × d directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Solve for the unknown x from the first proportion completely before substituting into the second proportion — don't try to combine both conditions simultaneously.

question: If 50% of 60% of 2/7 of a number is 618, find the number.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 7210.

 

GIVEN

 

• 50% of 60% of (2/7) of a number N = 618.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 50% of 60% = 0.5 × 0.6 = 0.3 = 3/10.

 

• So (3/10) × (2/7) × N = 618 ⇒ (6/70) × N = 618 ⇒ (3/35) × N = 618.

 

• N = 618 × 35/3 = 206 × 35 = 7210.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Combine all the given fractions/percentages into one single fraction first (3/10 × 2/7 = 3/35), then simply multiply the result by the reciprocal (35/3) to isolate N.

 

NOTE

 

• Converting percentages to fractions (50% = 1/2, 60% = 3/5) before multiplying often keeps the arithmetic cleaner than working with decimals.

question:
A shopkeeper sold a pen for ₹150 and made a profit of ₹30. Find the cost price of the

pen.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹120.

 

GIVEN

 

• Selling price (SP) = ₹150. Profit (in ₹) = ₹30.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Profit = SP − CP ⇒ CP = SP − Profit = 150 − 30 = ₹120.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For a rupee (not percentage) profit or loss, just add/subtract directly: CP = SP − Profit, or CP = SP + Loss.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse a rupee-value profit with a percentage profit — no percentage formula is needed here, just simple subtraction.

question:
A train 1386 m long is running at 18 km/hr. How long will it take to clear a 564 m long

platform completely?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 390 seconds.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = 1386 m. Platform length = 564 m. Speed = 18 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert speed: 18 km/hr = 18 × 5/18 = 5 m/s.

 

• To completely clear the platform, the train must cover (its own length + platform length) = 1386 + 564 = 1950 m.

 

• Time = distance/speed = 1950/5 = 390 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• '18 km/hr' converts neatly to exactly '5 m/s' (a very common speed in these questions) — remember ×5/18 to convert km/hr to m/s instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• To 'completely clear' any object (platform, bridge, another train, a pole), the train must travel its own length PLUS the object's length — a pole/man of negligible length only needs the train's own length.

question:
Two pumps, M and N, can fill a tank in 36 hours and 45 hours, respectively. Another

pump P can empty the tank in 30 hours. First M and N are opened, and after 8 hours, P

is also opened. The tank will be filled up in total T hours. The value of T is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 44.

 

GIVEN

 

• M fills the tank in 36 hrs, N in 45 hrs. P empties it in 30 hrs. M and N run first; P joins after 8 hours.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take total tank capacity = LCM(36, 45, 30) = 180 units.

 

• Rate of M = 180/36 = 5 units/hr. Rate of N = 180/45 = 4 units/hr. Rate of P = −180/30 = −6 units/hr (emptying).

 

• In the first 8 hours, only M and N work: filled = (5 + 4) × 8 = 72 units.

 

• Remaining to fill = 180 − 72 = 108 units.

 

• After P joins: combined rate = 5 + 4 − 6 = 3 units/hr. Time to fill remaining 108 units = 108/3 = 36 hours.

 

• Total time T = 8 (initial) + 36 (with P) = 44 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Use LCM of all given times as the total 'units' of work/tank — this converts every rate (filling or emptying) into a clean whole number, making multi-stage pipe problems much faster to track.

 

NOTE

 

• Emptying pipes/pumps always contribute a NEGATIVE rate; add them algebraically (subtract) when combined with filling pipes.

question:
The total surface area of a sphere is 6006 cm² less than the total surface area of a

hemisphere. If the ratio between the radii of the hemisphere and sphere is 5 : 3, then

find the radius of the sphere.

(Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 21 cm.

 

GIVEN

 

• TSA(hemisphere) − TSA(sphere) = 6006 cm². Ratio of radii, R(hemisphere) : r(sphere) = 5 : 3. π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let R = 5k (hemisphere radius) and r = 3k (sphere radius).

 

• TSA of hemisphere = 3πR². TSA of sphere = 4πr².

 

• 3πR² − 4πr² = 6006 ⇒ 3π(5k)² − 4π(3k)² = 6006 ⇒ 75πk² − 36πk² = 6006 ⇒ 39πk² = 6006.

 

• πk² = 6006/39 = 154 ⇒ k² = 154 ÷ (22/7) = 154 × 7/22 = 49 ⇒ k = 7.

 

• Radius of sphere r = 3k = 3 × 7 = 21 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Express both radii in terms of a single variable using the given ratio right at the start — this converts a two-unknown problem into a single-variable equation, avoiding messy simultaneous equations.

 

NOTE

 

• TSA of a solid hemisphere = 3πR² (curved surface 2πR² + flat circular base πR²); TSA of a sphere = 4πr² — do not confuse the two formulas.

question:
After selling an article at a discount of 4%, the profit percentage obtained is 20%. What

is the markup percentage?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 25%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Discount = 4% on marked price (MP). Resulting profit = 20% on cost price (CP).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let CP = 100. Since profit = 20%, SP = 120.

 

• Since SP is obtained after a 4% discount on MP: SP = MP × 0.96 ⇒ 120 = MP × 0.96 ⇒ MP = 120/0.96 = 125.

 

• Markup % = (MP − CP)/CP × 100 = (125 − 100)/100 × 100 = 25%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Markup% formula: MP = CP × (100+profit%)/(100−discount%). Here MP/CP = 120/96 = 1.25, i.e. markup = 25% directly, in one step.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Markup' is the percentage added to CP to fix the marked price, while 'discount' is subtracted from MP to get SP — always keep these two percentage bases (CP vs MP) distinct.

question:
If ₹8,404 is divided between Rishi and Yash in the ratio 7 : 15, then find the share of

Yash (in ₹).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. ₹5,730.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total amount = ₹8,404, divided between Rishi and Yash in ratio 7 : 15.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total parts = 7 + 15 = 22.

 

• Yash's share = (15/22) × 8404.

 

• 8404 ÷ 22 = 382 (value of 1 part).

 

• Yash's share = 15 × 382 = ₹5,730.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Divide the total by the sum of ratio parts first to get the value of '1 part', then multiply by the required person's ratio number — cleaner than multiplying the fraction directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check that the total divides evenly by the sum of parts (8404/22 = 382 exactly here), which confirms the arithmetic is on track.

question:
The price of 1 kg of carrot on Monday is ₹40. If it is increased by 5% and 3% on the next

two consecutive days, then what is its price (in ₹) on Wednesday?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹43.26.

 

GIVEN

 

• Price on Monday = ₹40. Tuesday's increase = 5%. Wednesday's increase = 3% (on Tuesday's price).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Price on Tuesday = 40 × 1.05 = ₹42.

 

• Price on Wednesday = 42 × 1.03 = ₹43.26.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For successive percentage changes, multiply the successive factors directly: 40 × 1.05 × 1.03 = 40 × 1.0815 = 43.26, without needing to compute the intermediate Tuesday price separately.

 

NOTE

 

• Successive percentage increases do NOT simply add up (5% + 3% ≠ 8% here); the net effect (8.15%) is always slightly more than the sum due to compounding on the already-increased value.

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for 'x', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', what will

come in place of question mark (?) in the following equation?

44 A 11 B 25 D 28 C 1 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 73.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Equation: 44 A 11 B 25 D 28 C 1 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 44 ÷ 11 × 25 − 28 + 1 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS: 44 ÷ 11 = 4. Then 4 × 25 = 100.

 

• 100 − 28 + 1 = 72 + 1 = 73.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the entire equation with the actual symbols first before calculating — this avoids sign confusion — then solve strictly by BODMAS (÷/× before +/−, left to right).

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is applying the letter-to-symbol substitution and the arithmetic simultaneously; always finish the substitution as a separate first step.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of

the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down

the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding

to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and

3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

(35, -34, 1)

(35, 14, 7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. (23, 266, 17).

 

GIVEN

 

• Sample sets: (35, −34, 1) and (35, 14, 7); find the option set following the same relationship.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test the rule: (third number)² = (first number) + (second number).

 

• Set 1: 1² = 1, and 35 + (−34) = 1. ✓

 

• Set 2: 7² = 49, and 35 + 14 = 49. ✓

 

• Check option D (23, 266, 17): 17² = 289, and 23 + 266 = 289. ✓ Matches perfectly!

 

• (Quick checks show none of options A, B, C satisfy c² = a + b.)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When two sample sets are given, look for a relation that fits BOTH before testing the options — squares, sums and products connecting the three numbers are the most common relations in this question type.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify a hypothesised rule against both given sample sets before applying it to the options, since a rule that works for only one set may be coincidental.

question:
In a certain code language,

P + Q means 'P is the husband of Q',

P # Q means 'P is the wife of Q',

P & Q means 'P is the brother of Q' and

P % Q means 'P is the father of Q'.

How is G related to E if 'G # V % M & H + E'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Husband's mother.

 

GIVEN

 

• + = husband of, # = wife of, & = brother of, % = father of. Statement: G # V % M & H + E.

 

SOLUTION

 

• G # V: G is the wife of V.

 

• V % M: V is the father of M.

 

• M & H: M is the brother of H (so M and H are siblings, children of V).

 

• H + E: H is the husband of E.

 

• Since V is father of both M and H, and G is V's wife, G is the mother of H.

 

• H is the husband of E, so from E's side, G (H's mother) is E's husband's mother.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each coded link into a mini family tree step by step (draw arrows), then read the final relationship directly off the tree from the required person's perspective.

 

NOTE

 

• Always work out gender and generation for each person as you decode the chain — 'brother' fixes M's gender as male, and 'husband' fixes H as male, which is essential to interpreting who is whose mother/father correctly.

question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-

digit numbers). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 4 1 1 7 2 4 1 2 7 4 4 9 6 3 9 1 6 1 9 2 2 8 8 (Right)

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an odd

digit and also immediately followed by an odd digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Two.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 4 1 1 7 2 4 1 2 7 4 4 9 6 3 9 1 6 1 9 2 2 8 8

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan each digit (except the two ends) and check if both its neighbours are odd:

 

• 3rd digit (1): neighbours are 1 (odd) and 7 (odd) → both odd. Count 1.

 

• 15th digit (9): neighbours are 3 (odd) and 1 (odd) → both odd. Count 2.

 

• All other odd digits in the series have at least one even neighbour, so they don't qualify.

 

• Total = Two.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every odd digit first, then simply check the digit immediately before and after each underlined digit — a fast visual scan avoids missing or double-counting positions.

 

NOTE

 

• Always exclude the first and last digits of the series from being 'the odd digit in question', since they have only one neighbour, not two.

question:
