Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are

alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to

that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. TYR.

 

GIVEN

 

• Letter-clusters: TYR, EJD, MRL, QVP.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the step pattern (letter-to-letter jump) within each cluster using alphabet positions:

 

• EJD: E(5)→J(10) is +5; J(10)→D(4) is −6.

 

• MRL: M(13)→R(18) is +5; R(18)→L(12) is −6.

 

• QVP: Q(17)→V(22) is +5; V(22)→P(16) is −6.

 

• TYR: T(20)→Y(25) is +5; Y(25)→R(18) is −7, not −6.

 

• EJD, MRL and QVP all follow the same +5, −6 pattern, but TYR breaks the pattern with −7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to their alphabet position numbers (A=1...Z=26) and find the step differences within each cluster — the odd one out will have a different step pattern from the rest.

 

NOTE

 

• Always test all four options for the SAME pattern before concluding — the odd one out is the one that breaks an otherwise consistent rule shared by the other three.

question:
Refer to the following series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single

digit numbers). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 8 7 7 4 2 1 5 4 8 9 4 1 1 1 9 9 3 7 9 5 4 (Right)

How many such odd digits are there each of which is immediately preceded by an odd

digit and also immediately followed by an odd digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 8 7 7 4 2 1 5 4 8 9 4 1 1 1 9 9 3 7 9 5 4

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scanning each digit (excluding the two ends) for both neighbours being odd:

 

• 12th digit (1): neighbours 4(even)... — check carefully: positions 12,13,14 are 1,1,1 and 15,16 are 9,9.

 

• Digit at position 13 (1): neighbours are 1 (odd) and 1 (odd) → qualifies. Count 1.

 

• Digit at position 14 (1): neighbours are 1 (odd) and 9 (odd) → qualifies. Count 2.

 

• Digit at position 15 (9): neighbours are 1 (odd) and 9 (odd) → qualifies. Count 3.

 

• Digit at position 16 (9): neighbours are 9 (odd) and 3 (odd) → qualifies. Count 4.

 

• Digit at position 17 (3): neighbours are 9 (odd) and 7 (odd) → qualifies. Count 5.

 

• Digit at position 18 (7): neighbours are 3 (odd) and 9 (odd) → qualifies. Count 6.

 

• Digit at position 19 (9): neighbours are 7 (odd) and 5 (odd) → qualifies. Count 7.

 

• Total = 7.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Where a long unbroken run of odd digits occurs (like the 1,1,1,9,9,3,7,9,5 run here), every interior digit of that run automatically qualifies — count them as a block instead of checking one by one.

 

NOTE

 

• Miscounting the exact number of repeated digits (e.g. missing a repeated '1') is the most common error in this question type — re-count the given series digit by digit carefully before solving.

question:
Seven boxes, M, N, O, P, Q, R and S, are kept one over the other, but not necessarily in

the same order.

Only P is kept above O. Only Q is kept between O and R. Only N is kept below S.

How many boxes are kept between M and N?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked. Only P is above O. Only Q is between O and R. Only N is below S.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only P is above O' ⇒ P is at the top (position 1) and O is at position 2.

 

• 'Only Q is between O and R' ⇒ from O (position 2), moving down with exactly Q between: position 3 = Q, position 4 = R.

 

• 'Only N is below S' ⇒ N is at the very bottom (position 7) and S is just above it (position 6).

 

• Remaining box M takes the only leftover position, 5.

 

• Final order (top to bottom): P(1), O(2), Q(3), R(4), M(5), S(6), N(7).

 

• Boxes between M(5) and N(7): only position 6, i.e. S — that's one box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert 'Only X is above/below Y' statements into fixed absolute positions immediately (top or bottom of the stack) — these are the strongest, most direct clues and should be placed first.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only N is kept below S' means N is the single box below S, i.e. S is second-last and N is last — not that there's just one box somewhere below S in general.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the

statements.

Statements: All Hats are Ratchets. No Ratchets are Cats. Some Cats are Angels.

Conclusion (I): No Hats are Cats.

Conclusion (II): No Angels are Ratchets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• All Hats are Ratchets. No Ratchets are Cats. Some Cats are Angels.

 

SOLUTION

 

• All Hats are Ratchets (Hats ⊆ Ratchets) + No Ratchets are Cats ⇒ combining an 'All' with a 'No' gives a valid 'No' conclusion: No Hats are Cats. So Conclusion I follows.

 

• No Ratchets are Cats + Some Cats are Angels: this only tells us some Cats (which are Angels) are definitely not Ratchets — it does NOT establish that no Angel at all can be a Ratchet (other Angels, not part of the 'Cats' overlap, could still be Ratchets). So Conclusion II does NOT necessarily follow.

 

• Hence only Conclusion I is valid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'All A are B' + 'No B are C' always gives 'No A are C' (a standard valid syllogism chain) — memorise this pattern to instantly validate conclusions like I.

 

• 'No B are C' + 'Some C are D' can only yield 'Some D are not B', never a universal 'No D are B' — this eliminates conclusions like II quickly.

 

NOTE

 

• Draw a quick Venn diagram when in doubt: it visually confirms that Angels could partly overlap with Ratchets outside the Cat-Angel overlap, so Conclusion II cannot be guaranteed.

question:
DR 12 is related to FK −6 in a certain way. In the same way, JM 18 is related to LF 0. To

which of the given options is KN 3 related, following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. MG −15.

 

GIVEN

 

• DR 12 → FK −6. JM 18 → LF 0. Find the pair related to KN 3 the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letter: D(4)→F(6) is +2. J(10)→L(12) is +2. Consistent: 1st letter shifts +2.

 

• 2nd letter: R(18)→K(11) is −7. M(13)→F(6) is −7. Consistent: 2nd letter shifts −7.

 

• Number: 12→−6 is a change of −18. 18→0 is also a change of −18. Consistent: number changes by −18.

 

• Apply to KN 3: K(11)+2 = 13 = M. N(14)−7 = 7 = G. Number: 3 − 18 = −15.

 

• Result: MG −15.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• With two coded examples given, always find and confirm the SAME shift pattern in both before applying it to the question term — this avoids being misled by a shift that only fits one example.

 

NOTE

 

• Keep letter shifts and the numeric shift as three completely separate, independent patterns — solve each one on its own rather than trying to find one unified formula.

question:
Refer to the following number and symbol series and answer the question that follows.

Counting to be done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) $ # # £ 9 % £ 7 * & € 1 3 4 5 6 4 9 € 2 5 & (Right)

How many such numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by a symbol

and also immediately followed by a symbol?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: $ # # £ 9 % £ 7 * & € 1 3 4 5 6 4 9 € 2 5 &

 

SOLUTION

 

• Identify each number and check whether both its neighbours are symbols:

 

• The number 9 (5th element): preceded by £ (symbol), followed by % (symbol) → both symbols. Count 1.

 

• The number 7 (8th element): preceded by £ (symbol), followed by * (symbol) → both symbols. Count 2.

 

• The number 1 (12th element): preceded by € (symbol), followed by 3 (a number) → does not qualify.

 

• The remaining numbers (3,4,5,6,4,9 in the middle run, and 2,5 near the end) each have at least one numeric neighbour, so none qualify.

 

• Total = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First mark every element as 'N' (number) or 'S' (symbol) above the series; then scanning for the pattern S-N-S becomes a quick visual search rather than a repeated mental check.

 

NOTE

 

• Long unbroken runs of numbers (like '1 3 4 5 6 4 9' here) can only ever contribute their two end-numbers as possible candidates, and even those need a symbol on the OTHER side too — check carefully.

question:
What will come in the place of '?' in the following equation, if '+' and '÷' are

interchanged and '−' and 'x' are interchanged?

195 + 3 x 22 - 6 ÷ 117 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 50.

 

GIVEN

 

• '+' and '÷' are interchanged; '−' and '×' are interchanged. Expression: 195 + 3 × 22 − 6 ÷ 117.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After interchange: + becomes ÷, × becomes −, − becomes ×, ÷ becomes +.

 

• New expression: 195 ÷ 3 − 22 × 6 + 117.

 

• Apply BODMAS: 195 ÷ 3 = 65. 22 × 6 = 132.

 

• 65 − 132 + 117 = −67 + 117 = 50.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the whole expression with the new (swapped) symbols FIRST, in one clean pass, before doing any arithmetic — this avoids accidentally reverting to the original symbols midway.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember it's a mutual swap (+ ↔ ÷ and − ↔ ×), not that each symbol changes to a completely new, unrelated one — double-check by re-reading the swap rule before substituting.

question:
Town P is to the west of Town Q. Town R is to the south of Town P. Town S is to the east

of Town R. Town T is to the north of Town S. Town Q is to the northeast of Town T. What

is the position of Town P with respect to Town T?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. Northwest.

 

GIVEN

 

• P west of Q. R south of P. S east of R. T north of S. Q is northeast of T.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Set P at the origin (0,0). Since P is west of Q, Q lies to the east of P, i.e. Q = (+x, 0) for some x > 0.

 

• R is south of P (same x as P): R = (0, −a) for some a > 0.

 

• S is east of R (same y as R): S = (b, −a) for some b > 0.

 

• T is north of S (same x as S): T = (b, −a+c) for some 0 < c < a, so T's y-coordinate is still negative (south of P's row) — this is consistent with the final clue that Q (at y = 0) is northeast, i.e. above and to the right, of T.

 

• So T has a positive x-coordinate (b) and a negative y-coordinate, while P is at (0,0).

 

• Relative to T, P is to the west (P's x = 0 < T's x = b) and to the north (P's y = 0 > T's y, which is negative).

 

• Combining west + north gives: P is to the Northwest of T.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Plot each town on a simple mental x-y grid (with north = +y, east = +x) as each clue is read — the final directional relationship then falls out directly from comparing coordinates.

 

NOTE

 

• The exact distances in such problems are rarely equal/unit steps; only track the SIGN (positive/negative, i.e. direction) of each coordinate, not precise magnitudes.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

121 123 127 133 141 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 151.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 121, 123, 127, 133, 141, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 123−121=2, 127−123=4, 133−127=6, 141−133=8.

 

• The differences increase by 2 each time (2, 4, 6, 8, ...), so the next difference is 10.

 

• Next term = 141 + 10 = 151.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever consecutive differences themselves form a simple arithmetic progression (here, +2 each time), just extend that secondary pattern by one more step to predict the next term instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always write out the difference row explicitly below the series — it makes second-order (difference-of-difference) patterns like this one immediately visible.

question:
Which of the following letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the

given series to make it logically complete?

ANF 17, DQI 21, GTL 25, JWO 29, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. MZR 33.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: ANF 17, DQI 21, GTL 25, JWO 29, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: A(1), D(4), G(7), J(10) — each increases by +3. Next = 10+3 = 13 = M.

 

• 2nd letters: N(14), Q(17), T(20), W(23) — each increases by +3. Next = 23+3 = 26 = Z.

 

• 3rd letters: F(6), I(9), L(12), O(15) — each increases by +3. Next = 15+3 = 18 = R.

 

• Numbers: 17, 21, 25, 29 — each increases by +4. Next = 29+4 = 33.

 

• Combining: MZR 33.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a multi-letter, multi-number cluster series into separate columns (1st letters, 2nd letters, 3rd letters, numbers) and find the pattern in each column independently — much simpler than trying to see one combined rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch that the letter step (+3) and the number step (+4) can be different from each other in the same series — don't assume they must match.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the

statements.

Statements: All curtains are blinders. All curtains are dividers. All curtains are walls.

Conclusions: (I) All blinders are walls. (II) Some walls are dividers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. Only conclusion (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• All curtains are blinders. All curtains are dividers. All curtains are walls.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Curtains ⊆ Blinders, Curtains ⊆ Dividers, Curtains ⊆ Walls (all three are separate 'All' statements sharing 'Curtains' as the common subject).

 

• Conclusion I ('All blinders are walls'): We only know curtains are a subset of both blinders and walls; nothing tells us ALL blinders (which may be a larger group than curtains) are walls. Does not follow.

 

• Conclusion II ('Some walls are dividers'): Since curtains are a common subset of both dividers and walls (Curtains ⊆ Dividers and Curtains ⊆ Walls), the curtains themselves guarantee an overlap — so 'Some walls are dividers' is definitely true. Follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a single group (here, Curtains) is stated to be 'All' of two or more other categories, it always guarantees a 'Some' relationship between those other categories — a very common and useful syllogism shortcut.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not assume that two categories which each fully contain a common third category must therefore have a full 'All' relationship with each other — only a 'Some' relationship is guaranteed.

question:
In a certain code language, 'mall tree army' is coded as 'vg ur ua' and 'plant army cup' is

coded as 'ti ud vg'. How is 'army' coded in the given language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. vg.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'mall tree army' → 'vg ur ua'. 'plant army cup' → 'ti ud vg'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The word common to both statements is 'army'.

 

• The code word common to both coded outputs is 'vg'.

 

• Since 'army' is the only word repeated in both sentences, and 'vg' is the only code repeated in both outputs, 'army' must be coded as 'vg'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In two-sentence coding questions, always find the common WORD between the sentences first, then find the common CODE between the outputs — that pairing gives the answer instantly, no need to decode the other words.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful to identify the single truly common word (here 'army' appears in both phrases) rather than accidentally matching a similar-looking but different word.

In a certain code language, 'photo vet scale' is coded as 'zk jh kv' and 'urn photo kin' is

coded as 'jh zn fl'. How is 'photo' coded in that language?

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-cluster pairs

are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster pair that

DOES NOT belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. QT - PT.

 

GIVEN

 

• Pairs: EH-DG, QT-PT, LO-KN, OR-NQ.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check the letter-position shift for both letters in each pair:

 

• EH → DG: E(5)→D(4) is −1; H(8)→G(7) is −1. Both shift by −1.

 

• LO → KN: L(12)→K(11) is −1; O(15)→N(14) is −1. Both shift by −1.

 

• OR → NQ: O(15)→N(14) is −1; R(18)→Q(17) is −1. Both shift by −1.

 

• QT → PT: Q(17)→P(16) is −1, but T(20)→T(20) is 0 (unchanged), breaking the pattern.

 

• So EH-DG, LO-KN, OR-NQ all shift both letters by −1, but QT-PT does not (second letter stays the same).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For letter-pair series, check BOTH letters' shifts independently — an odd one out often has just ONE letter breaking an otherwise uniform shift pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• Don't assume a matching first-letter shift is enough to confirm a pair belongs to the group — always verify the second letter's shift as well.

question:
BGLQ is related to EJOT in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the

same way, FKPU is related to INSX. To which of the following is HMRW related,

following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. KPUZ.

 

GIVEN

 

• BGLQ → EJOT. FKPU → INSX. Find the term related to HMRW the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check each letter's shift in BGLQ → EJOT: B(2)→E(5) is +3; G(7)→J(10) is +3; L(12)→O(15) is +3; Q(17)→T(20) is +3. All shift by +3.

 

• Confirm with FKPU → INSX: F(6)→I(9) is +3; K(11)→N(14) is +3; P(16)→S(19) is +3; U(21)→X(24) is +3. Consistent.

 

• Apply +3 to each letter of HMRW: H(8)+3=11=K; M(13)+3=16=P; R(18)+3=21=U; W(23)+3=26=Z.

 

• Result: KPUZ.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once a uniform shift (here +3) is confirmed across ALL letters using both given examples, simply add that same shift to every letter of the new word — no need for separate per-letter reasoning each time.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the shift pattern using BOTH given example pairs before applying it, in case the shift only coincidentally matches for one of them.

question:
GENU is related to KZRP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the

same way, OUVK is related to SPZF. To which of the given options is WKDA related,

following the same logic?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. AFHV.

 

GIVEN

 

• GENU → KZRP. OUVK → SPZF. Find the term related to WKDA the same way.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check GENU → KZRP letter by letter: G(7)→K(11) is +4 (1st, odd position); E(5)→Z(26) is −5, i.e. 5−5=0→wraps to 26=Z (2nd, even position); N(14)→R(18) is +4 (3rd, odd position); U(21)→P(16) is −5 (4th, even position).

 

• Pattern: odd positions (1st, 3rd) shift +4; even positions (2nd, 4th) shift −5 (wrapping around the alphabet where needed).

 

• Verify with OUVK → SPZF: O(15)+4=19=S ✓; U(21)−5=16=P ✓; V(22)+4=26=Z ✓; K(11)−5=6=F ✓. Confirmed.

 

• Apply to WKDA: W(23)+4=27→wraps to 1=A; K(11)−5=6=F; D(4)+4=8=H; A(1)−5=−4→wraps to 22=V.

 

• Result: AFHV.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When a coded shift takes a letter 'below A' or 'past Z', simply wrap around the 26-letter alphabet by adding/subtracting 26 — treat the alphabet as circular for this type of question.

 

NOTE

 

• Alternating shift patterns (like +4 for odd positions, −5 for even positions here) are less common but must be checked whenever a single uniform shift doesn't fit all letters.

question:
Seven people, B, C, D, I, J, K and L, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre

of the table. I sits fourth to the right of J. Only two people sit between B and C, when

counted from the left of B. D sits third to the left of K. L is an immediate neighbour of K

and C. How many people sit between I and L, when counted from the left of L?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Four.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people around a circular table, facing centre. I is 4th to the right of J. Exactly 2 people sit between B and C (counted from B's left). D is 3rd to the left of K. L is an immediate neighbour of both K and C.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Place J at a reference position (say position 0) and number positions 0–6 clockwise (facing-centre 'right' = clockwise). I = J + 4 = position 4.

 

• Testing the remaining clues systematically (only two people between B and C from B's left; D third to the left of K; L neighbouring both K and C) gives the unique consistent arrangement (clockwise from position 0): J, K, L, C, I, D, B.

 

• Check: B is 3 positions clockwise from C's position going the long way, i.e. exactly two people (D, I) sit between B and C counting from B's left (counter-clockwise) — ✓. D is third to the left of K (K→J→B→D, three steps) — ✓. L sits between K and C, adjacent to both — ✓.

 

• Now, counting from I towards L via the left (counter-clockwise) direction: I → D → B → J → K → L. The people between I and L in this direction are D, B, J and K — that's four people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular seating puzzles with 'right'/'left' clues, fix ONE person's position as a reference point first, assign clockwise = right, and convert every other clue into a position number relative to that reference — this keeps the puzzle systematic and avoids sign errors.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Third to the left of K' means 3 full steps counter-clockwise from K, landing exactly on D — not that D is anywhere within the first three counter-clockwise seats.

question:
A, B, C, D, W, X, and Y are sitting in a straight line, facing the north. Only two people sit

to the right of X. Only two people sit between X and C. Only two people sit between A

and D. D sits to the immediate left of X. B sits to the immediate right of Y.

Who sits at the third position from the left end of the line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. W.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people in a row, facing north. Only 2 sit right of X. Only 2 sit between X and C. Only 2 sit between A and D. D is immediately left of X. B is immediately right of Y.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two sit to the right of X' ⇒ X is at position 5 (positions 6, 7 are to its right).

 

• 'D is immediate left of X' ⇒ D is at position 4.

 

• 'Only two sit between X and C' ⇒ C is 3 positions from X(5); since position 8 doesn't exist, C = position 2.

 

• 'Only two people sit between A and D' ⇒ A is 3 positions from D(4); A = 1 or A = 7. Testing shows only A = 1 leads to a fully consistent arrangement.

 

• Remaining positions {3, 6, 7} are for B, W, Y, with 'B sits immediate right of Y' ⇒ Y = 6, B = 7 (the only consecutive pair available), leaving W = 3.

 

• Final arrangement (left to right): A(1), C(2), W(3), D(4), X(5), Y(6), B(7).

 

• The third position from the left end is W.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Place the person with the most specific clue ('only two to the right of X' fixes X's absolute position) first, then chain in the relative clues (immediate left/right) before tackling the 'people between' clues.

 

NOTE

 

• When a 'between' clue gives two possible positions (like A = 1 or 7 here), test both and keep only the one where every other clue can also be satisfied without contradiction.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

319 320 323 328 335 ?
solution_text:

GIVEN

 

• Series: 319, 320, 323, 328, 335, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences between consecutive terms: 320−319=1, 323−320=3, 328−323=5, 335−328=7.

 

• The differences form the odd-number sequence 1, 3, 5, 7, so the next difference is 9.

 

• Next term = 335 + 9 = 344.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Recognising the difference pattern as consecutive odd numbers (1,3,5,7,9...) lets you predict the next difference instantly without recomputing from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• Always write the difference row underneath the series — it converts a seemingly irregular series into an obvious, simple pattern.

question:
Refer to the following number, symbol series and answer the question. Counting to be

done from left to right only. All numbers are single-digit numbers.

(Left) Ω 9 % 6 1 * £ 5 # 2 8 $ 7 & + @ 3 4 (Right)

How many such symbols are there, each of which is immediately preceded by another

symbol and also immediately followed by a number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: Ω 9 % 6 1 * £ 5 # 2 8 $ 7 & + @ 3 4

 

SOLUTION

 

• Check every symbol (except the very first, which has no element before it) for: previous element is a symbol AND next element is a number.

 

• £ (7th element): preceded by * (symbol) ✓, followed by 5 (number) ✓ → qualifies. Count 1.

 

• @ (16th element): preceded by + (symbol) ✓, followed by 3 (number) ✓ → qualifies. Count 2.

 

• All other symbols (%, *, #, $, &, +) fail either the 'preceded by symbol' or 'followed by number' condition.

 

• Total = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every symbol that is immediately preceded by another symbol first (a smaller filtered list), then from that shortlist check only which ones are also followed by a number — two-step filtering is faster than checking both conditions simultaneously for every symbol.

 

NOTE

 

• The very first element of the series can never qualify as 'preceded by a symbol' since it has no element before it at all.

question:
Seven boxes B, C, D, I, J, K and L are kept one over the other but not necessarily in the

same order. Only C is kept below I. Only four boxes are kept between C and J. L is kept

between J and D. B is kept at one of the positions above J. How many boxes are kept

between K and C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 boxes stacked. Only C is below I. Only 4 boxes between C and J. L is between J and D. B is above J.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only C is below I' ⇒ I is second from the bottom (position 6) and C is at the very bottom (position 7).

 

• 'Only four boxes are kept between C and J' ⇒ J is 5 positions from C(7); J = position 2 (positions 3,4,5,6 lie between, i.e. 4 boxes).

 

• Remaining positions {1, 3, 4, 5} are for B, D, K, L.

 

• 'B is above J(2)' ⇒ the only position above 2 is 1, so B = position 1.

 

• 'L is kept between J and D' — testing the remaining positions {3,4,5} for D,K,L, the only fully consistent placement is D = 4, L = 3 (directly between J=2 and D=4), leaving K = 5.

 

• Final order (top to bottom): B(1), J(2), L(3), D(4), K(5), I(6), C(7).

 

• Boxes between K(5) and C(7): only position 6, i.e. I — that's one box.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix the absolute top/bottom positions from the strongest clues ('only X is below Y' type) before working on the relative 'between' clues — it narrows down the possibilities fastest.

 

NOTE

question:
If 'A' stands for '÷', 'B' stands for 'x', 'C' stands for '+' and 'D' stands for '−', what will

come in place of question mark (?) in the following equation?

16 B 3 D 36 A 18 C 18 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 64.

 

GIVEN

 

• A = ÷, B = ×, C = +, D = −. Equation: 16 B 3 D 36 A 18 C 18 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Substitute the symbols: 16 × 3 − 36 ÷ 18 + 18 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS: 16 × 3 = 48. 36 ÷ 18 = 2.

 

• 48 − 2 + 18 = 46 + 18 = 64.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Rewrite the equation with actual symbols in one clean pass, then apply BODMAS strictly (division/multiplication before addition/subtraction, left to right).

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check the letter-to-symbol key each time (A=÷, B=×, C=+, D=−) since these letter-symbol codings are frequently reshuffled between questions in this set.

question:
A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. D sits third to

the right of C. C sits second to the left of F. A sits third to the right of B. B sits to the

immediate left of E. How many people sit between A and D when counted from the left

of D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• 6 people around a circular table, facing centre. D is 3rd to the right of C. C is 2nd to the left of F. A is 3rd to the right of B. B is immediately left of E.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number positions 0–5 clockwise (facing-centre 'right' = clockwise). Let C = 0. D = C + 3 = position 3.

 

• 'C is second to the left of F' ⇒ F = C + 2 = position 2 (2 steps clockwise from C).

 

• Remaining positions {1, 4, 5} are for A, B, E, with A = B + 3 and E = B + 1.

 

• Testing B = 4: A = 4+3 = 7mod6 = 1; E = 4+1 = 5. All three positions {1,4,5} used exactly — consistent!

 

• Final arrangement (clockwise from 0): C(0), A(1), F(2), D(3), B(4), E(5).

 

• Counting from D towards A via the left (counter-clockwise) direction: D(3) → F(2) → A(1). Only F lies between them.

 

• So exactly one person (F) sits between A and D counted from the left of D.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Fix any one person's position as 0 and convert all 'right'/'left of' clues into simple +/− position arithmetic (mod the total number of people) — this keeps circular arrangements error-free.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Counted from the left of D' specifies the DIRECTION to travel (counter-clockwise here) — always travel in the specified direction only, not the shorter arc by default.

question:
Gagana starts from Point A and drives 5 km towards east. She then takes a left turn,

drives 3 km, turns left and drives 2 km. She then takes a right turn and drives 7 km. She

takes a final left turn, drives 3 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and

towards which direction should she drive in order to reach Point A again?

(Note: All turns are 90° turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 10 km towards south.

 

GIVEN

 

• Start A(0,0), facing east. Path: 5 km east → left → 3 km → left → 2 km → right → 7 km → left → 3 km → stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Start at A(0,0), facing east. Drive 5 km east: reach (5, 0), still facing east.

 

• Left turn (east→north), drive 3 km north: reach (5, 3), facing north.

 

• Left turn (north→west), drive 2 km west: reach (3, 3), facing west.

 

• Right turn (west→north), drive 7 km north: reach (3, 10), facing north.

 

• Left turn (north→west), drive 3 km west: reach (0, 10) = Point P.

 

• Distance from P(0,10) to A(0,0) = 10 km, directly along the y-axis, i.e. straight south of P.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only net east-west (x) and net north-south (y) displacement using coordinates as each leg is added — the final direction back to the start is read directly from the sign of the final (x, y) position.

 

NOTE

 

• For a 90° left turn, the facing direction rotates counter-clockwise (east→north→west→south→east); for a right turn, it rotates clockwise (east→south→west→north→east) — keep this rotation direction consistent throughout.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

37 49 61 73 85 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 97.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 37, 49, 61, 73, 85, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the common difference: 49−37=12, 61−49=12, 73−61=12, 85−73=12.

 

• The series increases by a constant 12 each time.

 

• Next term = 85 + 12 = 97.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When all consecutive differences are identical, it's a simple arithmetic progression — just add the common difference once more to the last term.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify the common difference across at least 3-4 consecutive pairs before concluding it's constant, to rule out a more complex hidden pattern.

question:
Which of the given letter-number clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the

following series to make it logically complete?

CFE10, GJI14, KNM18, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. ORQ22.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: CFE10, GJI14, KNM18, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• 1st letters: C(3), G(7), K(11) — each increases by +4. Next = 11+4 = 15 = O.

 

• 2nd letters: F(6), J(10), N(14) — each increases by +4. Next = 14+4 = 18 = R.

 

• 3rd letters: E(5), I(9), M(13) — each increases by +4. Next = 13+4 = 17 = Q.

 

• Numbers: 10, 14, 18 — each increases by +4. Next = 18+4 = 22.

 

• Combining: ORQ22.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split into separate columns (1st letters, 2nd letters, 3rd letters, trailing number) and find each column's own constant step — here all four columns conveniently share the same step of +4.

 

NOTE

 

• Even when all parts share the same numeric step, always verify each column separately rather than assuming — some series intentionally use different steps for letters vs. the number.

question:

Additional Information

question: The Republic Day celebrated on 26 January 2025, was India's ________ Republic Day.

question:

question:

solution_text:
The correct answer is 59%.

• India is divided into four seismic zones (Zone II, III, IV and V) as per the Seismic Zoning Map prepared by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS), with Zone V being the most seismically active (e.g. the Himalayan belt, North-East India, Kutch region).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

• Major earthquake-prone regions arise mainly due to India's tectonic position on the Indian Plate, which is continuously colliding with the Eurasian Plate, causing the Himalayas to rise and generating frequent seismic activity.

 

• The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) coordinates earthquake preparedness and mitigation efforts across vulnerable states.

 

NOTE

 

• 89%, 30%, 40% (Options B, C, D): These do not match the officially released figure of 59% vulnerable area as per the Ministry of Earth Sciences' March 2025 data.

question:
NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) which was scheduled to be launched from

India in July 2025 jointly by National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and

Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is a $1.5 billion mission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar), launched from India in 2025, is a joint Earth-observation satellite mission of NASA and ISRO, and it is billed as an approximately $1.5 billion mission, making it one of the most expensive Earth-observation satellites ever built. (निसार — नासा-इसरो संयुक्त पृथ्वी अवलोकन उपग्रह मिशन)

 

• NISAR uses dual-frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar — an L-band radar from NASA and an S-band radar from ISRO — to provide all-weather, day-and-night imaging of Earth's surface for monitoring ecosystem disturbances, ice-sheet collapse, natural hazards and groundwater changes.

 

• The satellite was launched aboard ISRO's GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• NISAR is designed to scan almost the entire globe every 12 days, providing consistent time-series data for monitoring changes in land and ice surfaces with unprecedented detail.

 

• This mission builds on a long history of India-US space cooperation, and it represents the two agencies' largest joint hardware collaboration to date.

 

• ISRO's other prominent Earth-observation and remote-sensing satellite series include the Cartosat, RISAT and Resourcesat programmes.

 

NOTE

 

• The option text in the answer key appears with a rendering glitch (e.g. '$C).5 billion mission'); the underlying correct value is $1.5 billion mission (Option C), reflecting the mission's substantial joint funding by NASA and ISRO.

question:
The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) in June 2025

________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2026.

• This landmark survey will help generate direct, reliable data on household income in India for the first time at a national scale — previously, income estimates were largely inferred indirectly through consumption expenditure surveys.

 

• The survey is expected to significantly improve policy-making, targeting of welfare schemes, and understanding of income inequality and distribution across the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• MoSPI is also responsible for conducting other key national surveys, including the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) and compiling GDP and other national accounts statistics.

 

• The last major Consumption Expenditure Survey results were released in 2022-23 (after a long gap since 2011-12), providing crucial updated data for calculating poverty and inflation indices.

 

• The National Sample Survey Office (NSSO), now part of the National Statistical Office (NSO) under MoSPI, conducts large-scale household surveys across India.

 

NOTE

 

• 2029, 2028, 2027 (Options A, B, D): Incorrect years — MoSPI's officially announced target year for launching this first nationwide household income survey is 2026, not any of these later years.
